title: Action registry (aiops.actions/v1)
description: Every action the agent may ever take: a named entry mapping to one Semaphore template, with typed extra-vars, a tier, a guard, a verify step and a rollback note. No registry entry = no action. The executor (10e1) may trigger only the templates listed here; the playbooks re-enforce the guard independently of the executor.

host_tiers.description: Inventory hostnames the mutating actions may target, by tier. Read by the playbooks (lookup of this file) AND by the agent. A host absent here is T2/T3 by default, i.e. never the target of a T1 action.

max_autonomy.description: Ceiling the registry allows for this action. Stage gates (10e approval, 10f auto) decide what is actually enabled; raising a ceiling is a reviewed PR. T0 actions are read-only so they may be auto; every mutator starts at approval (or none) until the 10f1 guards exist.

idempotent.description: true only if replaying the action is provably safe (see `idempotency`). Does not by itself raise max_autonomy.

idempotency.description: Why replay is safe, citing the repo mechanism.

template.description: Semaphore template name; defined in terraform/semaphore/templates.tf.

playbook.description: Repo-relative playbook the template runs; must exist.

applied.description: false = defined in Terraform but not yet applied (operator gate).

task_fields.description: Semaphore task fields the executor must set (not extra-vars). Values may reference extra_vars as {name}.

extra_vars.description: Typed extra-vars the executor may pass (Semaphore task `environment`). Anything not declared here must be rejected by the executor.

fixed_vars.description: Extra-vars the executor always sets to a constant (distinguishes actions sharing a template).

allowed_units.description: host -> systemd units restart-unit may touch.

requires_prior.description: Another action that must have run (and succeeded) first.

needs.description: Tooling/credential the template relies on (documented, not enforced here).

verify.description: Post-condition. `self` = the action's own AIOPS_RESULT must satisfy `expect`; `action` = run that (T0) action afterwards and require `expect` on its result.
